an experimental result. A concrete endpoint, assay, species, formulation,
exposure, condition, or structural mismatch can outweigh it. Do not invent a
numeric similarity score or a universal transfer cutoff.

Apply symmetric evidentiary standards. A valid direct positive outcome supports
the positive class and a valid direct negative outcome supports the negative
class; neither requires an additional speculative mechanism. Missing,
ambiguous, indirect, or nontransferable evidence is neutral rather than evidence
for either class. Use the query physicochemical prior only as a tie-breaker when
the transferable experimental evidence is genuinely balanced or sparse.


The decision is skin sensitization or contact allergy versus no sensitization.
Prefer validated human or in vivo sensitization outcomes and accepted integrated
outcomes. An adequately exposed validated negative sensitization result is
affirmative no-risk evidence; a validated positive result is affirmative risk
evidence. AOP key events may modify confidence when coherent and transferable,
but irritation, corrosion, phototoxicity, generic injury, permeability, or one
mechanistic event alone cannot define the label.
